content:
# What Decisionate does

Decisionate brings selected evidence from business datasets together so a team
can understand changes, choose an action, record its result and retain the
lesson. Explore relationships compares activity in one system with outcomes in
another. Business impact analysis estimates the impact of a recorded action using an
unaffected comparison and before-and-after history, when the evidence passes
the required checks. Correlation alone does not establish cause and effect;
an impact estimate depends on the comparison and stated business assumptions.
questions: What is Decisionate for?
Where did Insights go?
title: What Decisionate does

content:
- Dashboard and Dashboards show supporting KPIs, trends, mappings and targets.
- Business Analysis is the on-demand analysis workspace. Multi dataset report opens by default;
  Single dataset report analyzes one source with the same report engine.
- Weekly Reports provides independently configured weekly
  performance reviews and email delivery. Navigate between the workflows in the
  sidebar, not a shared page tab bar.
- Forecasts estimates future values and presents validation information.
- Relationships maintains saved two-metric, cross-source monitors.
- Decisions is the central place to create and track accountable actions.
- Action Needed organizes follow-up for existing decisions.
- Datasets and Connections manage evidence and imports according to permissions.
- Alerts manages weekly report recipients, schedule and delivery preferences.
- Help & Support provides guidance and a support, bug or feature request form.

Business Analysis was also called Analysis and Instant analysis.
Business impact analysis was previously labeled Assess a decision.
Business Analysis appears under the Analysis sidebar group; the group name is unchanged.
Weekly Reports replaces Weekly Review and Weekly Business Review in navigation.
Explore relationships is the correlation workflow; Business impact analysis is the
business-impact workflow. Existing analysis/report URLs and saved snapshots
remain valid; these names do not merge the two workflows or their settings.
questions: What is Decisionate for?
Where did Insights go?
title: What Decisionate does

content:
Insights is no longer a separate analysis destination. Old Insights links
redirect to Business Analysis. The dashboard Analysis tab and its panels were removed;
they should not be restored as a troubleshooting step. Business Analysis contains metric
findings, anomalies, relationships, limitations and decision evidence together.

The advanced relationship explorer and its dedicated worker were also retired.
Historical evidence may remain readable, but that is not a new advanced-analysis
service. Use the multi dataset report for current multi-metric analysis.
questions: What is Decisionate for?
Where did Insights go?
title: What Decisionate does

content:
A recommendation is evidence for human review, not an executed decision.
Decisionate does not automatically increase advertising budgets, alter a source
system, or guarantee business improvement when an analysis finishes.
questions: What is Decisionate for?
Where did Insights go?
title: What Decisionate does

content:
# Get to your first useful analysis

Start with a business question that needs evidence from more than one source,
such as whether changes in advertising spend are associated with changes in
orders. Do not compare raw spend amounts and order counts as equivalent units.
questions: How do I start?
How can I compare advertising with orders?
title: Get to your first useful analysis

content:
1. Sign in, complete workspace setup if prompted and check the active workspace.
2. Upload a supported file in Datasets or configure an available connection.
3. Wait for a successful import. Inspect actual columns and available dates.
4. Review the dataset's saved metric selection and business objective. Keep the
   measures relevant to the question; date and dimension fields are separate.
5. Open Business Analysis and choose Multi dataset report.
6. Select approved metrics from at least two datasets. Review each Date column
   and any Dimension column filter.
7. Enter a useful report name and business question. Choose dates and grouping
   consistent with the actual frequency and overlapping history of the sources.
8. Choose Preview analysis. Read coverage, anomalies, relationships and limitations
   before treating a finding as actionable. Save a snapshot when appropriate.
9. Create the business action centrally in Decisions, attaching the saved report
   when it supplies the evidence. Record an expected result and review date.
questions: How do I start?
How can I compare advertising with orders?
title: Get to your first useful analysis

content:
An empty metric list is not a reason to select arbitrary IDs or every numeric
column. Check the source import and dataset selection first. An unavailable
connector, incomplete backfill, insufficient observations or restricted role can
limit a workflow without meaning that the underlying business has no activity.

Twelve monthly source observations remain twelve observations even if you
select a year of dates or daily grouping. More historical data may be needed.
questions: How do I start?
How can I compare advertising with orders?
title: Get to your first useful analysis

content:
# Accounts, workspaces and access

A workspace is the boundary for datasets, connections, report evidence,
decisions, alert settings and AI context. Always check the workspace name before
analyzing data, changing settings or sharing a link.
questions: Why is access restricted?
Why can I not see another workspace's datasets?
title: Accounts workspaces and access

content:
Workspace owners manage configuration such as members, connections and billing
where permitted. Members can analyze authorized data and work with decisions,
but do not receive owner configuration access merely by joining a workspace.
Client-workspace access and agency access have their own controls.

The API enforces access; showing a navigation item or knowing an object URL is
not sufficient authorization. A workspace owner is not automatically a platform
administrator. Platform Admin is an internal, separately authorized surface.
questions: Why is access restricted?
Why can I not see another workspace's datasets?
title: Accounts workspaces and access

content:
1. Confirm the account and active workspace are the intended ones.
2. Check whether the page is an owner configuration page or an analysis page.
3. Ask the workspace owner to review membership or an invitation if necessary.
4. If a previously accessible workspace disappears, report the page, time and
   expected access through Help & Support. Do not try another person's IDs.

Changing a URL, copying a dataset ID from another workspace, or asking a chatbot
to ignore access restrictions cannot grant access. If content from an unrelated
workspace appears, stop sharing or changing it and report a possible security
incident without distributing the exposed data.
questions: Why is access restricted?
Why can I not see another workspace's datasets?
section: Missing datasets or a restricted page
title: Accounts workspaces and access

content:
Report and chart selections refer to the active workspace. An old browser tab
or bookmark may point to a different context. Switch using authorized controls
and reopen the relevant page rather than assuming an old link proves access.
questions: Why is access restricted?
Why can I not see another workspace's datasets?
title: Accounts workspaces and access

content:
# Agency and client workspaces

An agency workspace and its client workspaces are distinct data contexts.
Agency ownership does not imply unrestricted access to every client's data.
The client owner controls the agency-owner access supported by the application.
questions: Can an agency owner see client data?
Whose logo do agency clients receive?
title: Agency and client workspaces

content:
Confirm that the client workspace exists, the client has accepted the appropriate
invitation and the required agency access has been granted. An authorized agency
owner can switch into that client's context for permitted analysis and decision
work. That context does not provide the client Data navigation for adding
datasets or connection parameters. Client owners normally work in their own
isolated workspace rather than an agency-wide workspace switcher.

Client users have the client-workspace data and analysis access supported for
their role. Granting agency-owner access remains a client-owner operation;
another client user or a support prompt cannot grant it implicitly.
questions: Can an agency owner see client data?
Whose logo do agency clients receive?
title: Agency and client workspaces

content:
Reports emailed to agency-managed clients use the managing agency's configured
logo, brand name and colors when available. The footer retains Powered by
Decisionate. Emails to business and agency workspace owners use Decisionate's
logo. Missing agency branding should be corrected in authorized settings, not
replaced by a fabricated logo or an unrelated workspace's identity.

An agency logo does not mean the message is sent from the agency's domain.
Client weekly reports use the platform sender address and an agency-specific
display name. See Report email format and branding for the distinction.
questions: Can an agency owner see client data?
Whose logo do agency clients receive?
title: Agency and client workspaces

content:
For an access mismatch, share the intended workspace and the customer-safe error
through support. Do not include passwords, OAuth credentials or other clients'
records. The chatbot must not impersonate a client owner or silently change
access on the agency's behalf.
questions: Can an agency owner see client data?
Whose logo do agency clients receive?
title: Agency and client workspaces

content:
# Upload and inspect datasets

The file workflow offers CSV, JSON, Excel and Parquet ingestion, subject to the
readers installed in the deployment. A dataset's real schema comes from its
file or connector output, not from a generic example shown in a conversation.
questions: Which files can I upload?
Why do the imported columns look different?
title: Upload and inspect datasets

content:
Use stable column names and a header row for CSV. Include a genuine date or
timestamp when you need trends, relationships or forecasts. Numeric measures
need consistent units. Categories such as campaign, product or region belong in
dimension fields rather than being forced into numeric measures.

After processing, inspect the dataset name, row count, preview, date fields,
detected numeric columns and selected metrics. A numeric-looking identifier is
not automatically a sensible metric. A file containing twelve monthly records
does not contain daily observations merely because a date selector offers days.
questions: Which files can I upload?
Why do the imported columns look different?
title: Upload and inspect datasets

content:
Check the file format, actual worksheet or payload, column headers and imported
date range. For connector datasets, also check sync and backfill status. A
provider may return no records for a valid query because the account, dates or
permissions differ from the intended source.

Do not invent missing values, automatically interpret absent rows as zero
activity, or rename an unknown column to a familiar vendor field. If a source
schema changed, review the saved metric and date selections before recalculating.
questions: Which files can I upload?
Why do the imported columns look different?
title: Upload and inspect datasets

content:
Dataset-level metric selection controls eligible analytical measures; a report
then chooses a subset of those measures. Non-metric date, category and identifier
fields can remain available for inspection or filtering without being plotted as
metrics. Removing a measure from a chart is not a guarantee that its raw source
column has been deleted from storage.
questions: Which files can I upload?
Why do the imported columns look different?
title: Upload and inspect datasets

content:
# Connector availability and setup

Use Connections to see the current deployment's connector catalog. A provider
appearing in the source registry does not prove that its integration is enabled,
authorized or usable for your account.
questions: Which connectors exist?
Is every listed integration enabled?
title: Connector availability and setup

content:
Registry families include analytics and advertising, CRM, accounting, commerce,
payments, database queries and file uploads. Examples include Google Analytics,
Google Ads, Search Console, Meta Ads, Salesforce, HubSpot, Shopify, WooCommerce,
Square, Stripe, QuickBooks, FreshBooks, Sage, Xero, Zoho Books and Lightspeed
series, plus PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server sources.

Lightspeed series are separate integrations, not interchangeable credentials or
schemas. The registry explicitly keeps Lightspeed K and O planned. Consult the
generated connector catalog for the exact registry inventory and Connections for
runtime availability. Do not infer availability from a marketing list or a
provider's own API documentation.
questions: Which connectors exist?
Is every listed integration enabled?
title: Connector availability and setup

content:
The reviewed registry contains these 27 source entries. This list includes file
and database sources; it is not a count of 27 enabled OAuth integrations.

| Family | Source entries |
| --- | --- |
| Files | CSV, Excel, JSON, Parquet |
| Databases | PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server |
| Analytics | Google Analytics, Google Search Console |
| Advertising | Google Ads, Meta Ads |
| Other business sources | Google Business Profile, HubSpot, Salesforce Sales Cloud |
| Accounting | QuickBooks, FreshBooks, Sage Cloud Accounting, Xero, Zoho Books |
| Payments | Stripe, Square |
| Commerce | Shopify, WooCommerce, Lightspeed Retail R-Series, Lightspeed Retail X-Series |
| Restaurant | Lightspeed Restaurant K-Series, Lightspeed Restaurant O-Series |

Required configuration and actual availability remain source/deployment-specific.
K-Series and O-Series remain explicitly planned. A listed source does not prove
that its provider grants access to a particular customer's account.
questions: Which connectors exist?
Is every listed integration enabled?
title: Connector availability and setup

content:
1. Choose a source actually available in Connections.
2. Provide the account, property, shop, company, tenant or object identifier
   requested for that connector. Use the provider account with appropriate access.
3. Complete authorization or enter credentials only in the designated controls.
4. Run the available connection/pull operation and inspect the resulting dataset.
5. Enable scheduled sync only after the manual result is correct.

Permissions, provider limits, regional support and available history can constrain
the result. A token refresh does not create new permissions or missing history.
If reauthorization is requested, use the connection's authorization workflow.

Never paste secrets into support chat. A chatbot should not guess provider API
versions, scopes or column names. A vendor-specific question not covered by the
reviewed source needs current official vendor documentation or human review.
questions: Which connectors exist?
Is every listed integration enabled?
title: Connector availability and setup

content:
# Initial sync, historical imports and retention

Connector ingestion prioritizes the latest 90 days. It then backfills up to a
rolling three years of history that the provider actually makes available.
These are requests and limits, not a guarantee of three years of usable records.
questions: How much history is imported?
Why is only recent data available?
Is older data deleted?
title: Initial sync historical imports and retention

content:
Historical work is checkpointed and split into chunks, with background history
chunks capped at 30 days. Manual connector requests longer than 90 days are also
chunked. This bounds each ingestion task rather than making a single unbounded
historical request. The worker resumes its recorded progress; repeatedly
reconnecting or starting full overlapping imports is not a way to speed it up.

A recent dataset can be visible before backfill is complete. Check connection
progress and the dataset's actual dates before evaluating a three-year forecast
or concluding that older activity is missing from the provider.
questions: How much history is imported?
Why is only recent data available?
Is older data deleted?
title: Initial sync historical imports and retention

content:
Connector records older than the rolling three-calendar-year cutoff are removed
by the connector retention flow. Records with unusable dates cannot safely be
classified as old and may be retained. A historical summary cannot recreate
discarded transaction-level details.

The anomaly model's three-year lookback only excludes older observations from a
fit; it does not itself delete rows. Uploaded files, subscription expiry and
backup copies have separate retention rules. Do not extend the connector rule
into a promise about every data type or immediate deletion from all backups.
questions: How much history is imported?
Why is only recent data available?
Is older data deleted?
title: Initial sync historical imports and retention

content:
Check status, authorization, selected source account and dates. Wait for queued
work to finish before retrying. If it remains stuck, provide the connection and
workspace context through support, without tokens or raw private payloads.
questions: How much history is imported?
Why is only recent data available?
Is older data deleted?
title: Initial sync historical imports and retention

content:
# Choose relevant metrics

Dataset metric selection determines which measures can participate in analytical
workflows. Report metric selection is a further subset chosen for a particular
business question. A date column or dimension does not need to be a selected
numeric metric to serve its own purpose.
questions: Why are only some metrics preselected?
Does changing the objective replace manual choices?
Why did my selection not save?
title: Choose relevant metrics

content:
Business objectives shape automatic recommendations. When using system defaults,
changing the objective should resolve recommendations for the new objective,
rather than keeping unrelated automatic choices from the previous objective.
Deliberate manual selections, including an explicitly empty selection, must not
be silently overwritten by default-policy updates.

Accounting, commerce and payment defaults are restricted to reviewed
receipt/invoice measures emitted by that specific source/resource. This does not
mean every numeric field is a default, that every connector emits the same
receipt, or that internal costs and exchange rates must become metrics.
questions: Why are only some metrics preselected?
Does changing the objective replace manual choices?
Why did my selection not save?
title: Choose relevant metrics

content:
Open dataset details, review the Business objective and recommendation/profile
information, choose the desired columns and save. Use Reset to system defaults
only when you intend to replace a manual selection. If a save is unconfirmed,
keep the draft and use the provided recovery control; do not assume a success
message or a failed request means the opposite without checking the saved state.
questions: Why are only some metrics preselected?
Does changing the objective replace manual choices?
Why did my selection not save?
title: Choose relevant metrics

content:
Check the actual column name, numeric values, source resource, currency metadata
and saved policy. Empty values are not fabricated into a numeric field. A new
policy or missing normalized source field may require an explicit defaults reset
or successful resync, but those steps should follow diagnosis rather than be
promised as a universal fix.

Selection reduces the analytical surface. It is not a promise that every raw
unselected source field is absent from ingestion or memory at all stages.
questions: Why are only some metrics preselected?
Does changing the objective replace manual choices?
Why did my selection not save?
section: When a metric does not appear
title: Choose relevant metrics

content:
# CRM and financial metric caveats

Use exact fields from the selected dataset. Provider documentation describes
possible fields; only inspection of an authorized dataset establishes which
fields and values that customer actually has.
questions: Is ProductQuantity a Salesforce field?
Why is TotalOpportunityQuantity missing?
Why can I not sum invoice totals for product rows?
Why does Lightspeed show only quantity?
title: CRM and financial metric caveats

content:
Reviewed Opportunity defaults include numeric Amount, ExpectedRevenue,
Probability and TotalOpportunityQuantity when present and eligible for the
selected objective/policy. Amount is estimated opportunity value, not necessarily
booked revenue. ExpectedRevenue is a weighted expected amount. Probability is
an estimated percentage, not an observed win rate and not a value to sum.

TotalOpportunityQuantity is the exact supported source name. Do not invent
ProductQuantity as an equivalent field. Quantity is opportunity-level context,
not proof that a per-product breakdown exists. A missing or entirely empty field
cannot be selected as a usable numeric metric; valid zeros and constants are not
the same as an absent field.
questions: Is ProductQuantity a Salesforce field?
Why is TotalOpportunityQuantity missing?
Why can I not sum invoice totals for product rows?
Why does Lightspeed show only quantity?
title: CRM and financial metric caveats

content:
Connector normalization can expand line items vertically rather than creating a
new horizontal set of columns for every item's position. This improves schema
stability but does not make an invoice-header total additive across every line.
Approved metric policies distinguish line amounts, document totals, distinct
counts and component-weighted ratios to avoid unsafe double counting.

A product filter that splits a transaction cannot arbitrarily allocate its
header total to the remaining lines. Choose a line-item measure or a
transaction-level dimension if the filter is rejected for splitting totals.
questions: Is ProductQuantity a Salesforce field?
Why is TotalOpportunityQuantity missing?
Why can I not sum invoice totals for product rows?
Why does Lightspeed show only quantity?
title: CRM and financial metric caveats

content:
Unresolved or mixed currencies can make a monetary metric ineligible. Do not
assume all money uses two decimal minor units, convert an already normalized
amount again, or infer profit/ROAS from unrelated totals. For Lightspeed, Zoho,
Sage or any other provider, inspect the exact series/resource and returned fields
before explaining a narrow default selection.
questions: Is ProductQuantity a Salesforce field?
Why is TotalOpportunityQuantity missing?
Why can I not sum invoice totals for product rows?
Why does Lightspeed show only quantity?
title: CRM and financial metric caveats

content:
# Dates, grouped periods and aggregation

Date selection, grouping and aggregation answer different questions. A Date
column identifies when source activity occurred. Start and End bound a manual
report. Analysis group by chooses the calendar buckets used for comparison.
questions: What is a grouped period?
Does daily grouping create more observations?
Why are two pages showing different totals?
title: Dates grouped periods and aggregation

content:
Daily, weekly, monthly and quarterly grouping collect observations into those
periods. One year of monthly records gives twelve monthly buckets. Choosing daily
grouping does not manufacture daily activity from monthly totals or fill missing
dates with trustworthy zeros.

Minimum historical observations counts usable matched grouped observations for
relationship testing. Reports and Relationships default to 52 observations and
daily grouping; valid saved settings are retained. A long form date range can still
have too few observations because the source is sparse, dates do not overlap,
filters remove rows, values do not vary or lagging removes matched pairs.
questions: What is a grouped period?
Does daily grouping create more observations?
Why are two pages showing different totals?
title: Dates grouped periods and aggregation

content:
Sum, average, minimum, maximum, count and curated policies have different
meanings. Use the policy appropriate to the measure. Ratios, distinct users,
opportunity probabilities, balances and document totals are not interchangeable
with additive sales amounts. Do not sum rates or repeated header totals just
because a chart can show a number.

Reports compare the selected window with the immediately preceding equal-length
window. Missing coverage may withhold a change; a zero comparison baseline may
make the percentage undefined. That is different from a measured zero change.
questions: What is a grouped period?
Does daily grouping create more observations?
Why are two pages showing different totals?
title: Dates grouped periods and aggregation

content:
Check that both pages use the same workspace, metric policy, date column, range,
dimension filter and grouping before comparing their values. Dashboards,
Forecasts, manual Reports and scheduled weekly Reports have separate time
controls. Weekly reporting follows completed weeks rather than retaining the
dates of the snapshot used as its template.

Analysis grouping is independent of weekly delivery. The weekly summary covers
the last completed Monday-Sunday week and checks daily coverage and unusual
changes. Its relationship analysis keeps the saved analysis grouping and lag
units. A weekly email can therefore include a monthly relationship analysis,
if enough matched monthly history is available. It does not relabel months as
days, change approved metric aggregation, or rewrite the saved snapshot.
questions: What is a grouped period?
Does daily grouping create more observations?
Why are two pages showing different totals?
title: Dates grouped periods and aggregation

content:
# Filter metrics by category values

A dimension is contextual information such as channel, campaign, product,
customer, location or region. It filters the rows contributing to a metric; it
does not become a numerical outcome merely by being selected.
questions: Can I use non-metric columns for channel analysis?
Does Search values apply the filter?
Does a filter apply to every dataset?
title: Filter metrics by category values

content:
1. On dashboards, open Filters beside the other controls. Business Analysis,
   Weekly Reports, Forecasts and Relationships provide their own date/dimension controls.
2. Review Date column and choose Dimension column.
3. Choose one or more Unique values from the dropdown. Search values narrows the
   list of choices; entering search text alone is not the selected-value filter.
4. Check the selected values and resulting data. Clear the dimension filter to
   return to all eligible rows. Closing a dashboard's Filters tab retains it.

The current report contract supports one dimension column per selected dataset,
with up to 50 selected values for that column. Report filters are dataset-local:
filtering one source's channel does not automatically find or filter equivalent
channels in another source. Relationships has independent filters for both sides.
Business impact setup instead offers one comparison dataset and one Unique value
for its dimension. Its Unique value control combines search and selection in one
dropdown. Type to filter choices, then select one; search alone does not change
the selected value. Selecting a different value replaces the current comparison
value. The decision supplies the outcome; any saved outcome segment is shown
read-only with a clear control. The comparison's Date column is beside Dimension
column; changing it preserves the decision's analysis period. The outcome Date
column is beside Outcome metric and starts with the saved selection. In Business Analysis,
deliberate history-range and grouping changes remain under Analysis settings.
Decision assessment controls are in Business Analysis, not Weekly Reports. Weekly monitoring
has its own dataset date and dimension selectors and automatic weekly dates and grouping.
questions: Can I use non-metric columns for channel analysis?
Does Search values apply the filter?
Does a filter apply to every dataset?
title: Filter metrics by category values

content:
Distinct option values reflect available data, not a universal category taxonomy.
Missing and empty-string values are different. Structured objects are not safe
scalar filter options. If a historical summary did not retain a dimension, its
raw category detail cannot be reconstructed by the selector.

A filter can reduce the overlap and observation count available to correlations
and forecasts. An empty result is not automatically a system failure or proof of
no business activity. Check spelling, selected values, source coverage and dates.
questions: Can I use non-metric columns for channel analysis?
Does Search values apply the filter?
Does a filter apply to every dataset?
title: Filter metrics by category values

content:
If a dimension splits line items belonging to the same invoice/order, retaining
a header total on only some lines can misstate the result. A rejected filter may
require a line-level metric or transaction-level dimension, not a forced bypass.
questions: Can I use non-metric columns for channel analysis?
Does Search values apply the filter?
Does a filter apply to every dataset?
title: Filter metrics by category values

content:
# Use dashboards for KPIs and charts

Dashboard and the selectable industry dashboards are supporting views of metrics
and trends. Use Reports for the integrated findings, anomalies and cross-dataset
analysis workflow. The removed dashboard Analysis tab is not a hidden setting.
questions: Where are dashboard filters?
Why did All and 5 years disappear?
Where is the dashboard Analysis tab?
title: Use dashboards for KPIs and charts

content:
Select the dataset and measures, then review the chart and any manual metric
mappings. Industry dashboard names describe a view, not proof that a connector's
schema contains every expected column. Confirm the mapping and units before
interpreting a tile as revenue, cost or conversion performance.

Open Filters for Date column and Dimension column. Unique values and Search
values narrow a segment. Date and dimension choices apply to the selected view;
closing the tab does not clear them. Change grouping and aggregation only when
appropriate to the actual measurement frequency and metric semantics.
questions: Where are dashboard filters?
Why did All and 5 years disappear?
Where is the dashboard Analysis tab?
title: Use dashboards for KPIs and charts

content:
New or reset dataset-backed dashboard views default to 1 year. Available period
choices are 1 month, 1 quarter, 6 months, 1 year, 2 years and 3 years. The former
5-year and All options were removed; legacy views using them resolve to the
one-year default. Other valid saved periods are retained. Forecasts and Reports
have their own date controls.
questions: Where are dashboard filters?
Why did All and 5 years disappear?
Where is the dashboard Analysis tab?
title: Use dashboards for KPIs and charts

content:
Targets are benchmarks, not proof that increasing a measure is desirable.
Compare the chart, KPI values and coverage within the same filtered window.
Save PDF exports the dashboard view where supported; it is not the same as a
weekly email or a saved report snapshot. Shared links have separate access and
refresh considerations. Do not publish a view until its active workspace,
filters, mappings and intended audience are correct.
questions: Where are dashboard filters?
Why did All and 5 years disappear?
Where is the dashboard Analysis tab?
title: Use dashboards for KPIs and charts

content:
# Build single and multi dataset reports

Business Analysis is the on-demand analysis workspace. Multi dataset report opens by
default; Single dataset report is available separately for one source. Weekly Reports
has its own page and settings, automatic dates, whole-week and daily checks,
and earlier relationship history grouped weekly.
Use the sidebar to move between these separate workflows; neither page has tabs
for the other workflow. Business Analysis has Build analysis and Analysis preview;
Weekly Reports has Report setup and Report preview.
Business Analysis uses approved
dataset metrics, date policies, anomaly detection and report snapshots.

New multi dataset reports open with **Explore relationships**. The correlation
method, minimum matching periods, timing and metric-pair settings
are available under the expanded Relationship analysis section. Under Analysis
type, choose **Business impact analysis** to review an existing decision.
Saved reports keep their original analysis type. Neither mode replaces
decision creation or decision review on the Decisions page.
questions: How do I select metrics from multiple datasets?
How do I choose one dataset and filter its metrics by dimension?
How many metrics and lag tests are supported?
Does preview create a decision?
title: Build single and multi dataset reports

content:
Open Business Analysis and choose Single dataset report. Under Dataset and
metrics, use the searchable Dataset dropdown to choose one source. Type its name
or connector to filter choices, including sources on later catalog pages. Search
does not select a dataset or load its data files. Before choosing, no source's
metrics or dimension controls are displayed. Afterward, select the metrics from
that dataset and review its preselected Date column. Choose Dimension column and
Unique values to restrict the rows included in the analysis. All rows keeps the
dataset unfiltered. A chosen dimension with no values blocks preview until values
are selected or the filter is cleared.

Changing Dataset clears the previous source's metrics, dimension filters, date
choices and calculated preview. Select the new source's metrics before previewing.
Removing all metrics leaves the chosen dataset visible. A saved single-dataset
analysis restores its dataset, selected metrics and dimension filter rather than
showing every workspace source. Unavailable sources remain explicit and retryable;
they are not replaced with another dataset. Dataset names load first, and only
the selected source's metric catalog is read in this workflow. More names can be
loaded with Load more datasets when the catalog is paginated.
questions: How do I select metrics from multiple datasets?
How do I choose one dataset and filter its metrics by dimension?
How many metrics and lag tests are supported?
Does preview create a decision?
title: Build single and multi dataset reports

content:
Open an existing decision and choose Assess business impact, or select Decision
to review in the report builder. This is one searchable dropdown: type a decision
name to filter its choices, then select the decision. Typing alone does not change
the selected decision. The decision's action and outcome metric are
reused, not entered as a second decision. The Edit decision pencil beside the
selected decision opens its Decision Details. Use it to update the original action
or outcome metric; it appears only after a decision is selected. If no outcome
metric was recorded, choose it in Decision Details first. Confirm when the action actually started;
the decision creation date is not assumed to be the implementation date.
When did you implement the change? means the real action date, not the date you
expect results. Do not shift it to make the result look better.

Timing from earlier analysis uses the decision's original saved correlation,
checking the changed driver and the result to measure. It does not use the
unaffected comparison to invent a delay. A timing guide is available only when
the same delay stands out across two separate earlier-history checks. The source
history must end before implementation and use matching outcome date, aggregation,
dimension filter and timezone settings. Same-period-only analysis does not prove
zero delay. Old snapshots without these checks cannot supply a verified delay.
If several earlier relationships qualify, choose which one informed the decision.
There is no numeric lag input. Unknown or inconsistent timing produces an

column does not silently replace the decision's period.

In Business Analysis, Analysis settings contains only the shared history range and grouping.

Details. Weekly Reports has no assessment tab or setup form. Minimum history

date range cannot invent overlap. Comparisons outside the selected decision period
are also blocked. Saved snapshots keep their stored date choices.

switch to metric monitoring after preview and save. Historical evidence is kept.

and can be removed deliberately. Report name and business question are editable

decision and saves its report snapshot. It does not create a new decision or
mark an outcome successful. Return to decision to review the assessment and
record the actual outcome and lessons yourself. Later reviews retain earlier
assessments; changed actions or outcome metrics mark older results as historical.
Archived decisions can show their history but cannot receive new assessments.
Old standalone impact snapshots remain readable; new assessments require an
existing decision.

The history must include dates before and after the change. At least 52 complete weeks before and
8 after are needed with weekly grouping; daily needs 90 before and 28 after,
and monthly needs 24 before and 6 after. A partial week or month, or a period crossing the
change date, is not counted. Missing comparison periods are not filled with zero.
The required later observations must also be available after the timing reference
date. For example, a two-week historical lead places this reference date two weeks
after implementation. This is not a promised date for results. The real implementation date stays fixed;
those first two weeks are not discarded or treated as zero effect. Early results,
later results and the overall estimate are reported separately. A daily lag keeps
its original days even when impact is grouped weekly. Later weekly results start
at the first complete week after the suggested date.

Waiting for enough results means there are too few complete later observations to
assess the change yet. Future dates and today's incomplete day do not count. Check
that your analysis history includes newer results; choosing an old snapshot does
not automatically extend its saved dates. Weekly reviews use their automatic
rolling history. Historical timing is advice, not a promise about when results
will arrive or proof of cause and effect.

There is no seasonal-business checkbox in Business impact analysis. The comparison
provides the expected baseline, with reliability checked on records before the action;

history. It must improve two earlier prediction checks before being used, and
the chosen baseline must then pass a separate held-back earlier-period check.

pattern cannot bypass missing-data, false-alarm, business-context or stability checks.
With shorter history, the report explicitly says that separate yearly differences
could not be checked reliably. Existing seasonal settings do not force or disable

The report answers whether the change appears to have helped, worked against the
goal, or remains unclear. It shows the estimated difference and a range, checks
earlier predictions and false alarms, and explains the next step in ordinary
business language. If the comparison fails the checks or other changes prevent
a fair comparison, no impact amount is presented. A range including zero means
the effect is unclear, not that the action definitely had no effect.
The range assumes the selected baseline is appropriate and does not cover every
uncertainty from choosing that baseline.

This is a model-based estimate under stated assumptions, not a randomized test
or automatic proof of cause and effect. New timed assessments compare actual
results with a baseline fitted before implementation; early and later results
can differ. They do not establish an exact causal delay, attribute an ad-spend
correlation alone, or rule out unknown concurrent events. Old standalone snapshots
can retain their original immediate, ongoing-level-change assumption. The main
answer is calculated directly, so an AI provider cannot invent
an impact amount or upgrade weak evidence. Details are available under the checks.
Supporting charts and unusual-change tables are kept in Supporting business
results, rather than crowding the main answer and decision links.

does not show Relationship findings. Its own comparison checks and estimated
impact are independent of the correlation settings. This applies to Business Analysis
and Weekly Reports. Reopened older impact snapshots also omit their

results. Timing, phase estimates and waiting status are included in weekly emails.

later deleted; new calculations cannot reuse a deleted or inaccessible source.

business change. Existing saved reports keep their original workflow.

content:
A report built with Business impact analysis starts with a direct answer, its
estimated difference and range, and what to do next. A range including no effect
means the result is unclear. A failed comparison gives no impact amount at all.
This is not a guarantee that the action caused the result.

Estimated change in the chosen result is the leading number, with its estimated
range and the time after the change that it covers. Actual result and Without the
change (estimated) show what is being compared. Rates and averages are labeled
per period, not as totals. An unclear result is not presented as a win. What to
do next remains visible, while the full calculation narrative, checks, earlier
history and assumptions are under What we checked and what could change the answer.

Its main chart compares the actual result with the model's estimate without the
change, initially in the result's original units. Switch between Actual and
Indexed beside the chart title. Indexed uses the first positive estimated
without-change value after the change as 100 for both lines, keeping the
actual-versus-estimated gap visible rather than normalizing each line separately.
That same baseline is retained when changing the visible history. If no positive
estimated baseline exists, use Actual instead. The dashed estimate is not observed data,
and the effect range is not a prediction band around each chart point. Check the
dates: the estimated difference covers the complete periods after the change,
while the supporting metric cards can cover the full before-and-after window.
The chart opens with After the change. Full history can show the earlier records
without changing the calculation or the saved assessment. The legend names the
actual result and the estimate without the change separately. The start of the
first measured period is not presented as a guessed implementation date.

Supporting business results contains the selected-metric charts, unusual
changes and metric movements, not a second correlation analysis. Relationship
findings are available in Explore relationships instead. Older impact snapshots
also omit their old relationship findings when displayed, without changing the
stored snapshot. These results support the main answer rather than replacing
it. Decisions and outcomes remains the place to open the central
decision workflow with this report's evidence.
Create decision opens the central decision form; it does not record a decision
until that form is submitted. Continue decision opens an existing unfinished
decision instead of creating another. The action is a highlighted button when
available. If report coverage is incomplete, the disabled action states which
dates lack usable dataset values. Saving a report does not make missing data
usable; a strong correlation or previous-period baseline is not required.

Read the metric movements, unusual changes, impact checks, follow-up
actions and limitations together. In Explore relationships, read the relationship
findings alongside the other evidence. A significant relationship is not required for
a period comparison to be useful; nor does it establish that a change caused
the business outcome.

content:
# Interpret relationships without assuming causation

Relationship analysis compares how selected metrics vary across matched calendar
periods. Pearson measures linear association. Spearman measures rank-based
monotonic association. Neither method proves causation or a complete business
explanation.
questions: Does correlation prove that ad spend caused revenue?
What happens with more than two datasets?
What decision can a relationship support?
title: Interpret relationships without assuming causation

content:
Business Analysis and Weekly Reports display the Correlation coefficient and Lag
(observed) directly on each included relationship finding, without opening the
detailed explanation. Relationships shows these values in the opened saved
result too. Positive lags include their time unit and metric order. A valid
same-period result shows 0 (same period); a missing coefficient is not displayed
as zero, and insufficient evidence does not imply zero lag.

Lag units follow the relationship analysis grouping, not the chart's detail:
weekly relationship history produces a lag in weeks even when the report week
is also shown day by day. A tentative lag is still an observed result, not a
dependable response time; check the accompanying timing warning.

Consider the sign and magnitude of the coefficient, matched observation count,
timing, significance information, coverage and warnings together. A coefficient
near zero is not proof that the systems are unrelated in every possible way.
A strong coefficient can reflect a shared trend, seasonality, duplicates or
mathematically related measures rather than an independent business influence.

Report relationships use historical context of at least 90 calendar days ending
at the report's end, or a longer requested window, with the matched-observation
threshold applied after grouping and filtering. Weekly relationships use their
own rolling history. The value being compared for last week's KPI is not simply
correlated across seven daily points without a historical check.

Significance is adjusted across tested pairs and lags where the supported
statistical backend and inputs permit it. An unavailable significance value must
not be described as a passing test. Time-series autocorrelation and selecting
the best observed lag still limit interpretation.

attributed sales, a guaranteed conversion delay, an optimal budget, profit or

# Timing, direction and minimum observations

Lag is the number of grouped calendar periods by which one series is shifted
relative to another. A lag of 2 means two days with daily grouping, two weeks
with weekly grouping, two months with monthly grouping, or two quarters with
quarterly grouping. It is not automatically a two-day conversion delay.

How do I set direction for a middle metric?
Why is a one-year report insufficient?
title: Timing direction and minimum observations

content:
Evaluate timing and Maximum lag are always available above Relationship
directions in multi dataset reports, without an enable checkbox. Choose which
metric leads for each cross-dataset pair, or leave that pair at Same-period
comparison only. Only directed pairs run positive-lag tests. A metric can follow
one metric and lead another; there is no need to assign one global direction to
the middle source.

Remove relationship pairs you do not want to analyze. Removed pairs are excluded
from relationship tests and cross-dataset movement contrasts, including in weekly
reports using that template. Restore a pair from Removed pairs to reuse its
previous direction. Removing a pair does not deselect its metrics: KPI and
anomaly analysis still assess each selected metric. Removing all pairs runs no
relationship tests. Removing a metric also clears exclusions involving it, so
reselecting that metric creates its pairs again.

The interface no longer offers Test both directions. Directional timing includes
lag zero and eligible positive lags up to the selected maximum of 12 periods.
The maximum is not a search of every day from 1 to 365. A pair left at
Same-period comparison only does not run positive-lag tests. A maximum lag of
zero also restricts every retained pair to its same-period test.

title: Timing direction and minimum observations

content:
Reports and Relationships share a default minimum of 52 matched observations
and daily grouping, not 52 dates in the form. Explicit saved grouping and
thresholds are retained, including the previously saved 24-observation setting.
The editable minimum remains 24; 52 is the new default, not a new lower bound. Twelve
monthly source points fail that threshold. Filtering, non-overlapping dates,
missing buckets and shifting for lag can reduce the usable pair further.
The minimum must still be met after lagging. Positive-lag searches therefore
need more source history than a same-period comparison at the same threshold.
Constant or otherwise unsuitable series can prevent meaningful correlation even
when the nominal point count is large enough.

New report lag tests shift calendar buckets before dropping missing pairs. They
do not treat two neighboring surviving observations as adjacent calendar days
when dates between them were missing. Group more finely only if the source has
real observations at that finer frequency; do not manufacture history to pass a
threshold.

The best observed lag is a historical association under the selected tests.
Business timing knowledge should guide the hypothesis, and later independent
observations or an experiment should test it.

content:
# Saved relationships versus report relationships

Relationships is a separate page for a saved monitor comparing two metrics from
different datasets. Multi dataset report is the broader review workflow with
multiple metrics, period movements, anomalies and cross-source findings.

title: Saved relationships versus report relationships

content:
Choose the left and right datasets and their metrics. Review both Date columns
and apply each side's Dimension column and Unique values independently when
needed. Set the period and aggregation to fit the business question, then check
the actual overlapping source dates.

New analyses on both pages default to Spearman, daily grouping, Sum aggregation
where applicable, 52 minimum historical observations, a maximum lag of 12 grouped
periods, and same-period comparison. Correlation method, Minimum historical
observations and Maximum lag are visible in Relationship analysis rather than
hidden in advanced options. Valid deliberately saved settings are retained.

Leave Relationship direction at Same-period comparison only to avoid positive-lag
tests. Choose either named metric as the leader to evaluate zero through Maximum
lag. Maximum lag is shown only for a directional search. Dataset labels and each
source's dimension filter retain their original identities when the second
metric leads. The 12-period maximum is the same for daily, weekly, monthly and
quarterly grouping; it is not an automatic conversion into days.

There is no new fixed-lag editor. Existing saved fixed-lag monitors retain their
original timing, shown as Saved fixed lag, until the user explicitly chooses a
new direction. Saved grouping and observation thresholds, including weekly
grouping and a 24-observation threshold, are not overwritten by the new defaults.

The observation minimum is enforced after filtering, grouping and lagging.
Insufficient observations produce insufficient data, not a usable correlation.
Observation and lag limits persist with each monitor and are reused for its
scheduled evaluation. Existing monitors without a saved history threshold use
24 for backward compatibility; newly created analyses default to 52. Read the
matched periods, timing, strength and credibility before
saving. Shared defaults do not make the two workflows identical: the saved
monitor retains its fixed/automatic timing and stability scoring, while Reports
supports multiple pairs and its report-specific calendar alignment and testing
limits. Neither workflow proves causation.

Should I deploy the old correlation worker?

content:
The Correlation coefficient panel names the result being measured. More history needed
means there are fewer matching grouped periods than this monitor requires; for
example, 12 matching monthly periods do not meet a saved minimum of 24. Overlapping
dates alone do not satisfy that minimum. The panel shows the matched and required
counts. Correlation unavailable can also mean the matched values cannot produce a
score, such as a metric that does not vary. Analysis unavailable instead indicates
that the source data or a saved filter could not be used; check the accompanying
message.

The coefficient and lag are visible in the opened result. Lag (observed) shows the
selected delay with its grouping unit and the metric order when the delay is
positive. A valid same-period comparison shows 0 (same period). A computed lag
with limited timing evidence remains visible with a tentative-timing warning;
insufficient evidence shows Not established rather than implying a zero lag.
A manual comparison shows Lag (selected comparison), not an estimated delay.
Detailed timing candidates remain available under View timing evidence.

Delete a saved relationship with its trash button in Saved relationships. Opening
the evidence does not add a second delete control. Deletion requires confirmation
and also removes the opened evidence if it belongs to that relationship.

together, or you need anomalies, a frozen report snapshot and related decision
outcomes. A saved two-metric monitor is not a multivariate causal model, and a
report's collection of pairs is not one either.

content:
# Unusual changes and seasonal businesses

Report anomaly detection assesses each selected metric separately. It runs
independently of whether relationship analysis finds an eligible or significant
pair. No unusual change detected is a valid outcome; it is not proof that a
worker failed.

Weekly reports assess the last completed Monday-Sunday in two ways: the whole
week against earlier complete weeks, and individual days against their daily
baseline. Each selected metric has separate results for both. A normal weekly
value can hide unusual daily ups and downs; a run of small daily changes can
produce an unusual week. Whole-week results include an expected range even
when the week is not unusual. Missing dates prevent a complete-week assessment;
they are not replaced with invented zero values.
questions: Is anomaly detection MAD or standard deviation?
Does the seasonal checkbox force a seasonal model?
Does no unusual change mean the engine failed?
title: Unusual changes and seasonal businesses

content:
The detector uses preceding history inside a rolling three-calendar-year cap.
An assessed block is held out of its own training data. It fits a robust trend
and, when Business has seasonal activity is enabled, considers supported calendar
patterns. Seasonal terms must improve past-only validation; the checkbox does
not force a seasonal model onto every metric.

Annual patterns need at least two preceding annual cycles plus validation data
and adequate coverage. Three years selected in a form does not guarantee that
three years of suitable observations exist. Missing source activity is not
automatically treated as measured zero, and holidays and promotions are not
automatically known events.
questions: Is anomaly detection MAD or standard deviation?
Does the seasonal checkbox force a seasonal model?
Does no unusual change mean the engine failed?
title: Unusual changes and seasonal businesses

content:
The primary variability measure is scaled median absolute deviation of held-out
baseline residuals. Standard deviation of residuals is a fallback when MAD is
too small. If both are effectively constant, the method records a constant
residual rather than pretending that a reliable non-zero spread exists.
This is not simply calculating the standard deviation of all raw values.
questions: Is anomaly detection MAD or standard deviation?
Does the seasonal checkbox force a seasonal model?
Does no unusual change mean the engine failed?
title: Unusual changes and seasonal businesses

content:
Review actual value, expected value, expected range, deviation, direction and
the history/model warnings. The displayed range is an exploratory anomaly
threshold, not a guaranteed confidence interval or proof of a business cause.
Limited history or unassessed observations must not be reported as no anomalies.

Check imports, filters, date choices and structural changes first. If the
change warrants action, create a human-reviewed decision and later record its
outcome. The lookback cap excludes old data from fitting; connector retention
is the separate process that can delete old source records.

content:
# Forecast a selected metric

Forecasts estimates future values using observed source history. It is separate
from Business Analysis, which reviews evidence and relationships over historical periods.
A projection is not a commitment that the business will achieve that outcome.
questions: How do I forecast a segment?
Why is my seasonal forecast trend-only?

title: Forecast a selected metric

content:
1. Open Forecasts and select the intended dataset and metric.
2. Review Date column beside Dimension column. Select Unique values if the
   forecast should cover a segment rather than all eligible rows.
3. Choose the history range, grouping and aggregation appropriate to the source.
4. Enable Business has seasonal activity when recurring calendar patterns matter.

little history even when the unfiltered dataset looks large.

and exceptional events can undermine a forecast. Do not infer promotions or
holidays that were not provided as facts.

should not silently satisfy it with a different calculation. Preserve the
selection, retry after a confirmed service recovery and escalate persistent

Open Weekly Reports in the sidebar. It requires usable metrics from at least
two datasets for delivery. Business Analysis is a separate page and does not
control the weekly report's dates or time grouping.
The pages do not share a workflow tab bar. Weekly Reports uses Report
setup and Report preview; Business Analysis uses Build analysis and Analysis preview.

Does choosing a template enable sending?

title: Configure a meaningful weekly report

content:
Open Analysis -> Weekly Reports. Select metrics, date columns, dimension filters,
business question, seasonal setting and relationship pairs. Choose Preview report.
Previewing calculates the draft without changing the saved weekly setup or sending email.
After a successful preview, choose Save changes. Each workspace has one current
weekly report. Saving replaces that report and its setup for future weeks,
even if you change its name; it does not create another active report.
The default name is Weekly Business Report, not a random identifier. You can
use a custom name; it stays the same when the report is updated. Existing
generated names are replaced in the current setup and future reports, while
historical reports and decision evidence keep their original names.
There is no separate Save snapshot or Save weekly settings action on this page.
Changing the setup requires another preview before saving. A failed preview or
save leaves the previously saved setup unchanged. If the reporting week, source
data or saved setup changes before saving, generate a fresh preview.
Weekly history contains sent reports and previously saved legacy reports, not
alternative active setups. Opening history does not replace the current setup.
Reports already sent and evidence attached to decisions stay unchanged when
the current report is replaced. Sent-report history is recorded automatically
for new deliveries; old delivery logs cannot reconstruct missing report contents.
Removed pairs remain excluded
from weekly relationship analysis, while their selected metrics still receive
KPI and anomaly analysis. Saving settings does not enable sending or change recipients.

A saved business analysis offers Copy selection to Weekly Reports. This is an
editable copy, not a live link. Non-weekly timing choices reset to same-period
comparison, with a default maximum of 12 weeks; a three-day lag is not converted
to three weeks. Preview and save the independent weekly setup before use.

Use Delivery settings or Alerts to check recipients, schedule, delivery preferences
and email readiness. Enable delivery only after confirming the intended audience.
A successful scheduler invocation means a job was queued, not that an email was
delivered. Check terminal analysis status and delivery history separately.

Send report now emails the current weekly report only to the workspace owner,
including the client owner in a managed client workspace. First preview and save
the current weekly report. Sending does not save unsaved changes. This one-time
send can run while scheduled delivery is paused;
it does not change recipients, enable delivery or replace a scheduled send.
Only authorized workspace managers can use it. If the owner's account has no
usable email address, sending is blocked rather than using another recipient.

Sending requires usable data from at least two selected datasets in the last
completed week. If the preview has insufficient coverage, Send report now is
disabled and shows the exact dates needed. Sync or upload data for that week,
then preview again. Historical demo files belong in Business Analysis; weekly
reports do not shift to the most recent dates in an old file. Saved weekly
settings load only their selected datasets, not unrelated workspace sources.

After a confirmed failure before delivery starts, a deliberate retry starts a
fresh attempt. If delivery might have started, check delivery history before
trying again. Uncertain status reads keep the same request to avoid duplicates.
When the server confirms report preparation stopped before delivery, the page
explicitly says no email was sent. Older attempts without that confirmation
remain conservative; they are not silently resent.

KPI targets are benchmark context for the digest and interpretation. Setting a
target does not by itself create a separate immediate threshold-triggered alert.
Use the current delivery settings rather than assuming every metric anomaly
causes an instant email.

content:
Each run reviews the latest completed Monday-Sunday week in the platform
reporting timezone, compared with the preceding week. The manual report's Start
and End are not a permanent weekly window. Historical context rolls with the
current run date and is capped at three years where used for weekly analysis.

The last completed week's charts and unusual-change checks use daily detail:
one point for each Monday-Sunday date. KPI totals still cover the full week and
are compared with the preceding full week. A separate Whole-week assessment
checks each selected metric's full-week value against its expected weekly range,
using earlier complete weeks and seasonal adjustment when supported. Daily
changes and whole-week results can differ: opposing daily changes may cancel
out, or small daily changes may add up to an unusual week. Incomplete weeks are
excluded rather than treating missing dates as zero. If there is not enough
usable weekly history, the whole-week assessment is labeled unassessed.
Both views are included in the preview and email, and supplied as bounded facts
for interpretation. Earlier relationship history is
grouped into complete weekly periods, ending on the Sunday before the report
week; daily points are not mixed into the weekly relationship series.
There is no manual Start/End or Group by selector on the weekly page. Relationship
defaults are Spearman, 52 minimum matched weeks, same-period comparison, and a
maximum directional lag of 12 weeks. The minimum can be changed independently
within allowed bounds. Lag zero compares the same week. The selected metric's
approved aggregation policy is preserved: weekly grouping does not turn every
metric into a sum. Per-metric anomaly results include seasonal support and history warnings.

Changing Business Analysis dates, daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly grouping, or timing
settings does not change the saved weekly settings. Changing weekly settings does
not alter Business Analysis or either workflow's saved snapshots.

content:

assessments in Business Analysis, or open Assess business impact from Decision Details.

or deleted. Their setup is read-only, with a Manage assessment in Business Analysis link.

same selected metrics. The existing weekly configuration is replaced only after
preview and Save changes; saved decision assessments and report history remain.

weekly configuration. Changes in Business Analysis do not silently update that configuration.

An existing assessment's weekly preview includes a short Decision update with
the assessment period and a link to the decision, when available. Its evidence
remains available under Assessment evidence. The weekly email retains its answer,
estimated range when available, and next steps. It keeps the original change date,
result and unaffected comparison. Its study uses weekly grouping, starting at the rolling
three-year cutoff and ending with the latest completed week. It needs at least
52 complete weeks before the change and 8 after, plus the other comparison checks.
This is separate from the email's seven-day KPI totals; it does not attempt to
estimate a business impact from seven days alone.
An impact report keeps its own comparison checks and anomaly detection, but
does not also run an exploratory correlation or include Relationship findings
in its preview or email. A monitoring configuration checks selected relationships.
Previewing or emailing a weekly report does not create a decision or overwrite
its outcome. Explicitly saving a linked assessment attaches it to the selected
decision. Existing standalone weekly studies can continue under their original
saved configuration; new assessments require selecting a decision in Business Analysis.

As old history leaves the three-year window, the study can lose enough earlier
data to support an estimate. The email then explains the missing evidence rather
than repeating an old number. The original saved snapshot remains unchanged.

# Create decisions and track outcomes

A decision records a concrete action, its reasoning, expected result and later
outcome. Reading a report, finding a correlation or generating an AI recommendation
does not automatically create an accountable decision.
questions: Why is a draft called Review joined evidence?
Should a report always create three decisions?
Why do unrelated metrics appear in a decision?
Does editing create a new decision?
title: Create decisions and track outcomes

content:
Open Decisions and use its creation entry. Name the decision for the actual
business action, replacing the generated unique starting label. Supply the
required action and evidence, expected outcome and review information shown by
the form. Attach a saved report when it provides the justification, or use the
supported manual dataset-linked workflow.

A report-linked decision should retain the selected evidence metrics, report
identity and relevant limitations, not expand to every metric in its datasets.
An outcome metric is a measurement choice within the supported evidence scope,
not a reason to include unrelated source columns.
questions: Why is a draft called Review joined evidence?
Should a report always create three decisions?
Why do unrelated metrics appear in a decision?
Does editing create a new decision?
title: Create decisions and track outcomes

content:
Edit an existing decision to update that record; do not create a new one merely
to change its wording. A shared default name is not evidence that two records
are identical. Report linkage, action, selected evidence, ownership and recorded
outcomes matter. Do not merge distinct decisions or discard outcomes because
their titles look similar.

Legacy Review joined evidence placeholders may be editable drafts with no actual
action recorded. A draft is not evidence that a business action occurred.
Decisions and outcomes is not supposed to contain a fixed number of records.

Should a report always create three decisions?
Why do unrelated metrics appear in a decision?
Does editing create a new decision?

content:
Business impact review is an assessment of this decision, not another decision.
Choose Assess business impact on the decision page. The report builder reuses
the recorded action and outcome metric, and asks for the actual action start
date, an unaffected comparison from another dataset and the business context.
The action date is independent of when the decision record was created.

Choose Save assessment to decision after reviewing the calculation. It attaches
one assessment to the existing decision and preserves its report snapshot.
Saving the same completed analysis again does not duplicate the assessment or
create a second decision. Assessment history stays on Business impact review.
The model does not overwrite your actual outcome, outcome status, notes or lessons,
and does not automatically complete or mark the decision successful.

Compare before and after is the older simple metric comparison, not the
cross-dataset impact model. Its percentage change is not a causal impact estimate.
Keep that distinction when recording what actually happened.

At review time, record the actual outcome, its status and a specific lesson.
Document confounding factors instead of claiming a change was caused by the
decision solely because it followed it. Historical learning uses recorded
workspace evidence; it is not automatic retraining of the model.

Archiving retains history and differs from permanent deletion. Use the available
authorized lifecycle controls and read confirmations. Deleting a report does not
delete the decisions linked to that report.
Deleting a report snapshot also keeps its attached impact assessment on the
decision. Deleting a source dataset or workspace removes derived assessments
using that data. Permanently deleting a decision removes its attached assessment
records; archived decisions retain their history. Read-only users can view only
assessments whose source datasets they are authorized to access.

# AI interpretation and rules fallback

The statistical engines compute metric comparisons, anomaly evidence and
relationship tests. AI interpretation explains the supplied evidence
and suggests risks or follow-up actions. The AI does not create missing
observations, change statistical results or prove a causal business explanation.
questions: Does a completed report mean AI ran?
Is an API key required to display the model name?
Why is rules fallback active?
title: AI interpretation and rules fallback

content:
Generate a fresh report preview to request interpretation automatically. There
is no Include AI interpretation checkbox in the report builder. This also applies
when editing an older report whose definition disabled interpretation. A
previously saved snapshot keeps its original narrative; opening it or adding
provider credentials does not rerun AI or rewrite its history.

Provider configuration, a supported model/endpoint, workspace AI credits and
service availability affect whether an external AI response can be obtained.
The current implementation supports an OpenAI provider adapter; this static
article does not certify a currently available model or a particular account's
provider access.
questions: Does a completed report mean AI ran?
Is an API key required to display the model name?
Why is rules fallback active?

content:
A source of rules means deterministic fallback, not an external AI response.
Missing configuration, an unsupported provider, exhausted credits or a failed
provider request triggers fallback for report previews without blocking the
computed metric, anomaly and relationship results. A
successful report or Configured status alone does not prove external AI ran.

Provider and model names can be displayed without an API key. A key is required
to call the provider, not to render those names. Customer users should not add
platform credentials or paste a secret into chat; configuration is an operator
responsibility.

findings and anomaly summaries rather than the full raw dataset or every trend
point. Relevant authorized decision outcomes and lessons can supply context.
Do not infer a provider's retention, training or data-processing policy from this
request shape. Consult current approved Privacy and Security information.

# Safe troubleshooting and support requests

operation. A generic unavailable message is not proof of data loss, an expired
subscription, an AI failure or a connector permissions problem.

title: Safe troubleshooting and support requests

content:
Open Help & Support and use Ask Decisionate for product guidance. You can ask a
follow-up question, expand a cited documentation section, or open its product
page. AI answers and documentation excerpts are labeled separately. If AI is not
configured or cannot answer, relevant documentation remains available. Missing
evidence is not permission to invent an answer.

Factual guidance is taken from approved documentation sections, not invented by
the model. If the documentation does not establish the answer, the assistant
says it cannot confirm it from the approved information available at this time.
If only part is documented, it shares that part with an explicit limitation.
Related documentation is not proof that an unlisted feature exists, is
unavailable, or is planned. An unrelated question may receive a polite redirect;
an unclear question may need clarification. A source review date is not proof
of your account's live state. Human support can investigate missing details.

Questions and recent user messages may be sent to the configured AI provider
with approved customer documentation. Do not include private business records or
credentials. The assistant does not query live datasets, inspect your account,
read internal runbooks, access GitHub or execute actions. Guidance does not use
your business-analysis AI credits. Usage limits can require you to wait.

The conversation stays in the current page rather than a saved chat history.
Clear conversation, leave the page or switch workspaces to start fresh. Clearing
the page does not erase information already processed by the provider. Stop
waiting cancels the browser request, not necessarily a provider call in progress.

Contact support opens the normal support form with the latest question for you
to review. It does not send an email automatically or attach the entire chat.

Does an unavailable message mean data was lost?

  save.

content:
# Joining periods and matching entities

Dashboard joins, entity matching and relationship tests serve different purposes.
A join combines evidence on a key such as a normalized period. Entity matching
groups records describing the same customer or product. Correlation studies
whether metric values vary together; neither other operation proves causation.
questions: How does a join differ from a relationship?
Does Entity Matching use fuzzy AI matching?
title: Joining periods and matching entities

content:
Open Compare data on a dataset dashboard with at least two available sources.
Choose datasets, source metrics and date columns, and apply each source's own
dimension filter if needed. Join selected data normalizes dates into comparable
periods. Check overlap, coverage, joined metric choices and mappings before
interpreting the chart. Reset joined data releases the joined analysis context;
review the restored selection before continuing.

No overlapping normalized dates, invalid date values or overly narrow filters
can prevent a useful joined comparison. A join does not create missing business
activity or make different currencies equivalent. Use Reports for a broader
multi-metric review and a frozen analysis snapshot.
questions: How does a join differ from a relationship?
Does Entity Matching use fuzzy AI matching?
title: Joining periods and matching entities

content:
Entity Matching selects source datasets, customer or product type, matching-key
columns and analytical measures. The current resolver uses exact normalized
identifiers, emails, phones, SKUs and names; it is not a general fuzzy or
AI-inferred identity service. Inspect the preview before saving the supported
canonical records and unified dataset.

Exact normalized names are weaker evidence than a trustworthy shared identifier.
Two unrelated source systems can reuse a local customer or product ID. Confirm
